method.growth: g_t = ln((S_t+1)/(S_t-4+1)) with S_t the 4-quarter sum

caveats: OpenAlex topic drift: topic assignments are re-derived over time, so a domain's paper counts are not necessarily measured on a single frozen topic snapshot.

CPC concordance noise: CPC boundaries do not align cleanly with human technology categories, so patent counts may over- or under-count a domain. Known overlaps include QEC subset-of quantum_computing and genAI/ai_agents subset-of AI's G06N3/00 group.
Jan-1 dating: patents with only a year (Jan 1 sentinel) and papers with coarse dates are assigned deterministically, which can shift a small number of records across quarter boundaries.
Grant-date lag includes pendency: the grant window is dated by issue date, so k-quarter alignment absorbs examination pendency (typically 1-3 years), not just inventive lag.

Multi-membership: a patent matching several domains is counted once per matched domain, so domains are not statistically independent, which makes the pooled bootstrap over domains mildly anti-conservative.
Rolling 4-quarter sums plus a 4-quarter lag consume 8 quarters per observation, so overlapping observations are strongly autocorrelated and effective sample size is far below the nominal point count.
